feedback.problem: Given a curve $x=\sqrt{{y}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(2,1)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\sqrt{{y}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\sqrt{{y}^{3}})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3/2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{y}^{1/2}-2{y}^{-3} \\  & =\frac{3{y}^{1/2}}{2}-\frac{2}{{y}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{3{y}^{7/2}-4}{2{y}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{2{y}^{3}}{3{y}^{7/2}-4}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(2,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(2,1)} \\  & =\frac{2(1)^{3}}{3(1)^{7/2}-4} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =-2(x-2) \\ y & =-2x+4+1 \\ y & =-2x+5.\end{aligned}
$$
